reconcile.note: Clarke orders all eight post-resurrection appearances into one sequence spanning forty days, placing Luke's ascension scene as the final event.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg tallies the span itself: Luke gives one day, John at least ten, Acts forty, and calls Luke/Acts the greatest discrepancy.

quotes.text: How long did Jesus remain on earth? Luke: One day ( xxiv ). John: At least ten days ( xx , xxi ). Acts: He was “seen of them forty days” ( i, 3 ). The greatest discrepancy is between Luke and Acts, two books which it is claimed were written by the same author.
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on John 20:26 and Acts 1:3.

sides.snippet: After eight days again his disciples were inside, and Thomas was with them.
sides.verseText: After eight days again his disciples were inside, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the midst, and said, \"Peace be to you.\"

sides.snippet: appearing to them over a period of forty days, and speaking about God's Kingdom.
sides.verseText: To these he also showed himself alive after he suffered, by many proofs, appearing to them over a period of forty days, and speaking about God's Kingdom.
